 Order

This writ petition is filed for following reliefs:
"a. Issue a Writ of Certiorari or any other writ or order quashing the impugned award vide KIADB/LAQ/975/2022-23, dated 07.12.2022, Annexure-F passed by respondent no.2 and approved by respondent no.4 and consequently AS.PLJr/JJP/1519/2022-23 and PLJr/ JJP/1564/2022-23 quash notice dated 09.01.2023 Annexure-D and E, b. Issue writ of mandamus directing the respondents to pass award as contemplated under the provisions of The Right to Fare Compensation and Rehabilitation Act 2013 as assured under Annexure-B in respect of lands belonging to the petitioners and or, c. Direct the respondents to pass award by following the procedure of section 29(2) of KIAD Act for payment of compensation by way of consent award in respect of the petitioners land and or, d. Issue any other writ or direction which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit in the circumstances of the case, including cost of this writ petition in the interest of justice and equity."

2. Sri S.G. Hegde, learned counsel for petitioners submitted that petitioners herein were owners of land bearing Sy.no.54/1, measuring 02 acres 28 guntas situated at Obalapura village, Thymagondlu Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District.

It was submitted that said land was notified for acquisition for formation of Multi Model Logistic Park (MMLP) project, under Preliminary Notification dated NC: 2023:KHC:41148 08.12.2020 and Final Notification dated 12.08.2021 despite petitioners objections.

It was submitted that though acquisition notifications were issued after coming into force of The Right to Fair Compensation and Rehabilitation Act 2013 (RFCTLARR Act), respondents- authority assessed compensation under provisions of Land Acquisition Act.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Rehabilitation Act 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: However, respondents were proceeded to pass award referring to Land Acquisition Act 1894 (LA Act), constraining petitioners to file this writ petition.

3. It was submitted that Division Bench of this Court in W.A.no.890/2022 and connected matters in BMRCL Vs. M/s Sri Balaji Corporate Services, had taken note of circular issued by respondent no.5 on 27.10.2016 resolving to pass award under provisions of RFCTLARR Act in all cases, where acquisition notifications were issued on or after 01.01.2014 and upholding directions issued by learned Single Judge for passing of award under provisions of said Act.

entities.text: BMRCL Vs. M/s Sri Balaji Corporate Services
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Relying upon same, learned counsel sought for passing similar orders in this case also.

4. On other hand, Sri Gopala V Bilamane, learned counsel for respondents no.2 to 4 sought to submit that insofar as passing of award by referring to provisions of RFCTLARR Act, Division Bench of this Court in W.A.no10038/2022 had granted interim order against order passed by learned Single Judge in NC: 2023:KHC:41148 W.P.no.108802/2016 issuing direction for passing of award under provisions of RFCTLARR Act.
It was submitted that since matter was pending before Division Bench, relief sought for by petitioners was liable for rejection.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was further contended that insofar as claim of compensation in respect of land in question,
respondent had received rival claims from Smt.Saradamma W/o late Sri Kempagiriyappa and Smt.D.K. Pushpalatha W/o Late Sri Kempagiriyappa, that they had filed suit in O.S.no.178/2021,
stated be pending before Senior Civil Judge & JMFC., Nelamangala.
Therefore, it was submitted that rival claimants were necessary parties to this writ petition and even on ground of non-joinder of necessary party, writ petition was liable to be dismissed.

6. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition record.
7.
From above submission, it is seen that there is no dispute about acquisition of land belonging to petitioners for formation of MMLP Project by respondent.

Though, petitioners were not questioning acquisition, their claim was that compensation was to be awarded by following principles of NC:
2023:KHC:41148 RFCTLARR Act.

Said claim is opposed only on ground that since acquisition notifications were prior to amendment of Section 30 of RFCTLARR Act by Act no.20 of 2022, which came into force from 05.04.2022, petitioners' claim was unjustified and contrary to ratio laid down in Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB, Mysuru & Anr. vs. Anasuya Bai (D) by Lrs. & Ors.1, and W.A.no.1415/2018 in Ananthaswamy Vs. State of Karnartaka & Ors.
8.

entities.text: Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB, Mysuru & Anr. vs. Anasuya Bai (D) by Lrs. & Ors.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Ananthaswamy Vs. State of Karnartaka & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Contention about rival claimants, need not be considered by this Court, since relief sought for in writ petition would apply to all claimants/rival claimants.

9. Insofar as main relief sought, it is seen that Division Bench of this Court in M/s Balaji Corporate Services's case (supra), has dealt with issue in detail and while upholding order passed by learned Single Judge, directed respondents to pass award under provisions of RFCTLARR Act.

Though learned counsel for respondents no.2 to 5 sought to place reliance on interim order passed by this Court in W.A.no.100388/2022, it is seen that against order passed in W.P.no.53718/2017 and connected matters, wherein KIADB was also a party, only 2017 (3) SCC 313 NC: 2023:KHC:41148 BMRCL, the beneficiary had preferred appeal and KIADB had accepted direction issued.

Hence,
ratio in M/s Balaji Corporate Services's case (supra) would apply to this case.
10. Consequently, Writ petition is allowed.

General award dated 07.12.2022 at Annexure-F and award notices at Annexures - D and E are quashed insofar as land measuring 02 acres 28 guntas in Sy.no.54/1, 02 acres 12 guntas in Sy.no.54/2 of Oblapura village are concerned.
Respondents to pass award under provisions of RFCTLARR Act, after issuing notice to petitioners and other interested persons.
